text_content: **Key Driver Insights, Demographic Breakdowns, and Prioritised People Action Plan (Q2–Q4 2025)**

Key driver analysis identified that Manager effectiveness has the strongest relationship to engagement (r=0.62), surpassing other measured drivers such as role clarity and recognition. This statistical relationship indicates that improvements in managerial practices are likely to yield the largest incremental gains in engagement enterprise-wide. Analysis used Pearson correlations on the Q2 2025 survey dataset with standard significance testing (p<0.01). Leadership should interpret r=0.62 as a substantive effect size and prioritise measurement of managerial behaviors, coaching frequency, and feedback quality as leading indicators to be tracked monthly through HR systems during Q2–Q4 2025.

100 for employees with tenure 5+ years, a 12-point gap that signals an onboarding and retention challenge. Regional breakdown shows APAC engagement at 74%, EMEA 72%, and North America 76%, while individual contributor engagement averaged 73% compared with 77% for managers. Gender distribution differences were within 2 percentage points. HR and Talent Analytics will prioritise targeted onboarding interventions and segmented reporting beginning 1 July 2025 to narrow these gaps, with executive sponsors.

The people action plan includes exactly 5 enterprise actions delivered by 31 December 2025. 1. Revise onboarding to 90-day program with milestones — Owner: HR; launch Q3 2025. 2. Publish transparent career pathways and promotion criteria — Owner: Talent; framework by 30 Sep 2025. 3. Deploy an enterprise recognition platform — Owner: Total Rewards; pilot Q4 2025. 4. Run monthly pulse surveys with rapid feedback loops — Owner: People Analytics; live 1 Oct 2025. 5. Deliver targeted wellbeing and retention interventions for high-risk cohorts — Owner: People & Culture; complete 31 Dec 2025.
